verdicts.reason: The text says outright that "no package is installed" during the workflow.
"the checkboxes in `tasks.md` are the record of implement's progress ... never a substitute" means the tasks must be ticked as the work is done in implement.
The later-edits column for `spec.md` and `checklists/requirements.md` says "no" after the specify stage.
The later-edits column for `plan.md`, `research.md` and the "Phase 1 files" says "no" after the plan stage.
`tasks.md` may be edited later "only by implement's `[X]` marks and by converge appending a `## Phase N: Convergence`", which is exactly the later_edits rule.
The table gives `convergence.md` and `convergence-2.md` as "converge, one per round" with later edits "no".
"Ignore files (`.gitignore`, `.dockerignore` and so on) stay untouched" directly forbids writing to them.
"Nothing of the workflow lands in `/testbed`: no spec copies, notes, summaries", so creating .md files in the repo breaks the rule.
The text names "A script written anywhere else — `/tmp/test_x.py` ... breaks this rule" as a violation, so the check forbids that case.
The text only explains that hints are "written for someone typing slash commands" and never states a ban on running `/speckit.*` commands, so the ban is only implied.
"quote it as it appears, marked `[UNVERIFIED — not fetched]`" directly sets the required link format.
"Where a template asks for the branch, write `001-issue`" directly sets the value of the Feature Branch field.
"Copy ... spec-template.md to `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY/spec.md`" requires the spec file to exist.
"Persist the feature directory to `/tmp/speckit-sdd/.specify/feature.json`" with `"feature_directory": "specs/001-issue"` defines the check.
"The spec directory and file are always created by this stage" requires the spec to exist.
"LIMIT: Maximum 3 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers total" directly sets max 3.
"Generate a checklist file at `SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY/checklists/requirements.md`" requires the checklist to exist.
"replace the marker in the spec with it" means no [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers may remain in the final spec.
"Once `SPEC_FILE` and `checklists/requirements.md` are written" assumes the spec exists.
"Once `SPEC_FILE` and `checklists/requirements.md` are written" assumes the requirements checklist exists.
